From: Anna Proctor <anna.proctor@medisys.com>

Cc: privacy@medisys.com
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Medisys SSQ workbook — provenance & subprocessor exhibits

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our procurement SSQ we need a compact set of exhibits that demonstrate how Redwood handles PII for our healthcare workloads. Can you please provide the following by EOD next week (or tell me if any of these require an NDA or redaction):

- A labelled dataflow diagram showing service boundaries, points where PII is tokenized/pseudonymized, and the custody of encryption keys.
- A current subprocessor inventory (CSV is fine) including region of processing, purpose, and whether they have access to plaintext PII.
- A short statement (1-2 paragraphs) on KMS custody and key split (who holds keys, whether we support customer KMS).
- Retention windows for: raw request logs, telemetry/metrics used for model optimization, and KV/prefix caches that might touch identifiers.
- Example audit log lines showing an operator access event (redacted is fine) and the S3-like artifact naming convention.
- Any cross-border transfer mechanisms or SCCs that apply for EU->US flows.

Attachments: We expect PDFs/CSVs; if you prefer a shared Drive folder we can accept that.

Primary contact here is me (Anna Proctor, Medisys — Privacy). If it helps, loop in your security or product folks. We may follow up with a short call after review.

Best,
Anna

Subject: Re: Medisys SSQ workbook — provenance & subprocessor exhibits

Anna — thanks for the clear list. We're assembling the artifacts now; I’ve attached the initial set and included notes inline below. If you need redaction we can produce a redacted bundle.

Attachments (attached to this message):
- dataflow_medical_pipeline_v2.pdf (diagram, compressed)
- subprocessors_inventory_2026.csv (columns: name, purpose, region, access_plaintext, contract_sla_rev)
- kms_custody-statement.txt (short explanation)

Quick answers / pointers:
- Dataflow diagram: the attached PDF highlights three zones: customer ingress (edge), transient inference runtime (GPU pools), and long-term telemetry/metrics store. PII is pseudonymized at ingress for our hosted API when customers opt into tokenization; the diagram annotates where prefix caches retain KV handles (not plaintext).
- Subprocessors: the CSV includes our cloud provider for object storage, managed KMS provider (optional for customers — we offer customer KMS integration), telemetry pipeline vendor (batch processing), and an opportunistic GPU provider for burst capacity. The CSV flags whether each subprocessor can access plaintext PII.
- KMS custody: see kms_custody-statement.txt — short version: default model keys are held by Redwood's managed KMS, customers can bring their own keys (BYOK) via supported KMS integrations; we support split custody for enterprise Private deployments (customer key + HSM-backed module).
- Retention: raw request logs (time-limited) default 30 days for hosted trials, configurable up to 90 days for enterprise; telemetry aggregates are retained 13 months by default for model regressions and cost analytics; KV caches for inference are ephemeral (TTL 24 hours by default) unless customer config pins a cache. All of this is captured in the attached CSV and annotated diagram.
- Audit log example: attached in the Drive link (we redacted user IDs). The log lines show operator id, action (kv_cache:flush, model:deploy), and artifact paths (s3://ri-prod/tenant-123/ingest/2026-09-29/...). We’ll pull a redacted sample if you need specific columns.
- Cross-border: for EU->US transfers we rely on our DPA with SCCs plus standard SCCs with cloud providers; for Dedicated/Private deployments we can restrict routing to EU regions. We call out region routing in the diagram.

Next steps: Marissa (CS) — can your team provide a redaction template (if Medisys needs elements removed) and confirm whether you want the full CSV or a filtered view (no vendor contact emails)? Dylan (Security) — can you prepare a redacted audit-log sample and a short justification of key-splitting for Private deployments?

If helpful I can also upload a short video walkthrough of the diagram. Happy to schedule a 30-min review next week.

Thanks,
Rafael

Thanks Rafael — looks good. A few operational asks from CS to keep the doc set thumb-friendly for procurement: 

- Please confirm the default 30d raw log retention applies only to hosted API customers on the free/standard tiers; for enterprise/Dedicated we set per-contract retention.
- For the subprocessors CSV: remove vendor POCs (emails) and include a "can_access_plaintext" boolean column and a "processing_location" column we can point the buyer to.
- Dylan — can you surface 3 anonymized audit lines that show: (1) admin key access event; (2) operator session replay; (3) object-store export action. Include field names we can map to Medisys' SSQ keys.

Operationally I propose: Rafael — we put the artifacts into a Medisys-specific Drive folder with a README that includes the redaction policy and a short index (1 page). I can draft the README and the redaction template this afternoon.

Marissa

Rafael / Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the artifacts posted to the shared Drive. I downloaded the PDF and CSV and skimmed the KMS statement; high-level questions / follow-ups: 

1) In the CSV, please flag which subprocessors have access to plaintext and add a column "data_purged_after_contract_end" (yes/no). We need this for our legal review.
2) For the dataflow diagram: can you add a callout showing how we can opt for BYOK + HSM split custody for model keys (so our Security team can see the exact handoff).
3) Audit logs: the redacted sample is fine — can the sample include the column headers in a separate CSV file (we need to map names to our SSQ fields)?
4) Can you record a short 8–10 minute walkthrough video (screen share) of the diagram and the subprocessor CSV? That will speed our legal review.

If you can get items 1–3 to us by COB Monday (5 Oct) and the walkthrough early next week that would be ideal. Otherwise propose a slot for a 30-min call next Tue/Wed (we're in PDT).

Thanks again — this is moving quickly on our side.

Best,
Anna
